alt: Poster: How F&O turnover is counted for tax audit - total of favourable and unfavourable differences, Rs 10,000 profit plus Rs 7,000 loss equals Rs 17,000 turnover, Section 44AB limits of Rs 1 crore and Rs 10 crore
text:
A Rs 10,000 F&O profit and a Rs 7,000 loss make Rs 17,000 of turnover, not Rs 3,000.

For tax audit under Section 44AB of the Income-tax Act, 1961, derivatives turnover is not the contract value. Per ICAI guidance on tax audit, it is the total of favourable and unfavourable differences on settled trades, so profits and losses are added together as absolute amounts rather than netted.

The audit limit for business turnover is Rs 1 crore. It rises to Rs 10 crore where cash receipts and cash payments each do not exceed 5% of the respective totals. Separately, Section 44AB(e) can require an audit regardless of turnover where a person who opted for presumptive taxation under Section 44AD declares lower profit and income exceeds the basic exemption limit.

Treatment of option premium and the other details can vary by case, so the computation should be confirmed with a Chartered Accountant.

Our reading: a high-volume year with a small net result can still cross the audit limit. This is an opinion, not advice.
